Job was blameless and prayed for his children regularly. How can you pray for those you love?
Satan asked, "Does Job fear God for no reason?" Why do you follow God?
Job lost everything in one day. How would you respond to such loss?
Job said, "The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord." How can faith hold in grief?
God allowed Job to be tested further but set limits. What does this show about God's control?
Job said, "Shall we receive good from God, and shall we not receive evil?" How do you hold both?
Job's friends sat with him in silence for seven days. How can you simply be present with someone suffering?
Job cursed the day he was born. What does it show that the Bible includes such honest lament?
Job asked why he was given life in such misery. What can you bring honestly to God?
Eliphaz reminded Job of how he had comforted others. How do we respond when we are the ones needing comfort?
Eliphaz assumed suffering comes from sin. Why can this be an unhelpful answer to suffering?
Eliphaz spoke of human frailty before God. What is true in his words, and what is missing?
Eliphaz said, "I would seek God, and to God would I commit my cause." What do you need to commit to God?
"Blessed is the one whom God reproves." How has God's correction been good for you?
Job said his grief was heavier than the sand of the sea. How can you let others share honest grief?
Job said friends should show kindness to the despairing. How can you be a faithful friend?
Job asked his friends to show him where he had erred. How do you listen to someone in pain?
Job described life as hard and brief. When have you felt this way?
Job said, "I will speak in the anguish of my spirit." How can you speak honestly to God?
Job asked, "What is man, that you make so much of him?" How does God's attention to you feel?
Bildad assumed Job's children died for their sins. Why is it harmful to assume we know the reasons for suffering?
Bildad urged learning from past generations. What wisdom have you learned from those before you?
Bildad said God will fill your mouth with laughter. What hope do you hold for the future?
Job asked, "How can a man be in the right before God?" How does the gospel answer this?
Job longed for someone to arbitrate between him and God. How does Jesus fill this need?
Job brought his complaint directly to God. How can you be honest with God?
Job said, "Your hands fashioned and made me... you have granted me life and steadfast love." What does God's care in making you mean?
Zophar spoke harshly to Job. How can we speak truth without harshness?
"Can you find out the deep things of God?" What does God's greatness mean to you?
Zophar spoke of hope and security when we turn to God. What hope do you need?
Job said the animals and birds teach that the Lord's hand has done this. What does creation teach you about God?
"With God are wisdom and might; he has counsel and understanding." How does this comfort you?
Job told his friends their silence would be wiser. When is it better to listen than to speak?
Job said, "Though he slay me, I will hope in him." What does that kind of trust look like?
Job asked God to show him his sins and not hide his face. What do you long to ask God?
"Man who is born of a woman is few of days and full of trouble." How does knowing life is short affect you?
Job said a tree can sprout again, but asked if a man can live again. How does the resurrection answer Job?
Job hoped God would call and he would answer. What does it mean to long for God?
Eliphaz accused Job of undermining fear of God. Why is it easy to misjudge people in pain?
Eliphaz asked, "Are the comforts of God too small for you?" What comforts of God have helped you?
Job called his friends "miserable comforters." How could they have comforted him better?
Job said, "My witness is in heaven." What does it mean that someone in heaven speaks for you?
Job said, "My spirit is broken." When have you felt this, and where did you find hope?
"The righteous holds to his way." What helps you hold on?
Bildad was impatient with Job's words. How can you be patient with someone's grief?
Bildad described the fate of the wicked. Why is this not the whole story about suffering?
Job felt abandoned by family and friends. Who might feel abandoned around you?
Job said, "I know that my Redeemer lives." What does this hope mean to you?
Zophar said the joy of the wicked is brief. Why does the success of the wicked trouble us?
Zophar spoke of the heavens revealing iniquity. Why might his true words still miss what Job needed?
Job asked why the wicked prosper. How do you wrestle with that question?
Job said his friends' comfort was empty. What makes comfort real?
Eliphaz said, "Agree with God, and be at peace." What does peace with God mean to you?
Eliphaz spoke of returning to the Almighty. Where might you need to return?
Job said, "Oh, that I knew where I might find him!" When has God felt hidden to you?
"He knows the way that I take; when he has tried me, I shall come out as gold." How does this help in trials?
Job treasured God's words more than his daily food. How do you value God's word?
Job saw the poor oppressed and asked why God seems silent. What injustice troubles you?
Job said God's eyes are on the ways of the wicked. How does this give hope?
Bildad asked how anyone can be pure before God. How does the gospel answer this?
Bildad said dominion and fear are with God, who makes peace in his high heaven. How does God's greatness bring peace?
Job asked his friend, "How you have helped him who has no power!" How can your words truly help the weak?
Job said these are "but the outskirts of his ways." What does God's power in creation show you?
Job held fast his righteousness and would not let it go. What does integrity in trials look like?
Job asked whether the godless will call on God at all times. What does it mean to delight in the Almighty?
People dig deep for silver and gold. What do people dig for most today?
"Where shall wisdom be found?" Where do you look for wisdom?
"The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom." What does fearing the Lord look like for you?
Job remembered when the friendship of God was upon his tent. When have you felt close to God?
Job helped the poor and the fatherless. How can you be eyes to the blind and feet to the lame?
Job said, "I cry to you for help and you do not answer me." What do you do when God seems silent?
Job wept for those in trouble. How does compassion for others shape your heart?
Job made a covenant with his eyes. How can you guard your eyes and heart?
Job treated his servants fairly because God made them too. How should this shape how you treat others?
Job shared his food with the fatherless. Who could you share with?
Job did not trust in gold. Where are you tempted to put your trust?
Elihu was angry that the friends had found no answer. Why is it hard to explain suffering?
Elihu waited for the elders to speak. What does it mean that wisdom comes from God's Spirit?
"The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life." What does it mean to live by God's breath?
Elihu said God speaks in different ways. How has God spoken to you?
Elihu spoke of a mediator and a ransom. How does this point to Jesus?
Elihu insisted God does no wrong. How do you hold onto God's goodness in hard times?
"His eyes are on the ways of a man." What does it mean that God sees all?
Elihu said to look at the heavens and see how high God is. What does God's greatness say about your troubles?
Elihu said people cry out but do not ask, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night?" What songs has God given you in the night?
"God is mighty, and does not despise any." What does this show about God?
Elihu said God delivers the afflicted by their affliction. How has God taught you through hardship?
"God is great, and we know him not." How do you respond to God's greatness?
Elihu described thunder, snow and rain as God's work. Where do you see God in the weather?
"Stop and consider the wondrous works of God." What wonder can you stop and consider today?
God asked Job, "Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?" What does this question stir in you?
God told the sea, "Thus far shall you come, and no farther." Where do you need God to set limits on chaos?
God asked who provides food for the ravens. How does God care for all creation?
God knows when the mountain goats give birth. What does God's knowledge of creation teach you?
God describes the strength of the horse and the flight of the hawk. What in creation amazes you?
Job said, "I am of small account; I lay my hand on my mouth." What does humility before God look like?
God asked Job, "Will you condemn me that you may be in the right?" How do you respond to God's greatness?
God made Behemoth. What does this show about God's power over creation?
God asked who can stand before him. What does this show about his supremacy?
"Whatever is under the whole heaven is mine." How does this shape how you hold your possessions?
Job said, "I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you." How has suffering deepened your knowledge of God?
God asked Job to pray for his friends. How can you pray for those who hurt you?
God restored Job's fortunes. What does the end of Job show about God?
